title: Optimal strategies for shadow tomography with limited resources
authors: Zhen-Peng Xu, Qi Ye, Jie Wang, Gereon Koßmann, Andreas Winter, René Schwonnek
abstract: Shadow tomography addresses the task of efficiently predicting many expectation values of an unknown quantum state from randomized measurements on comparatively few copies. Existing analyses promise large scaling advantages, but the optimal strategies realizing these guarantees are not always known, and the required measurements are potentially challenging to implement on current hardware. We address this gap for Pauli observables by computing optimal sample-complexity parameters and constructing optimal measurement strategies under realistic resource constraints. We focus on memoryless protocols, where each copy is measured only once, and on measurements with bounded interaction range. Our approach reduces the problem to the analysis of graph parameters of the frustration graph encoding the Pauli anticommutation relations. We provide efficient numerical methods for the general case and analytically prove that Clifford measurements are optimal in many situations. This includes all perfect graphs, all single-qubit, all two-qubit measurement scenarios, and more. Applied to Hamiltonian energy estimation, our framework yields constructive strategies and improved variance bounds for molecular benchmarks.
summary: This work develops optimal strategies for shadow tomography by mapping the required measurement resources onto graph parameters derived from Pauli observables. It establishes theoretical bounds on sample complexity using concepts like fractional chromatic number and provides constructive methods for estimating molecular Hamiltonians with improved variance estimates.
main_problem: The paper addresses shadow tomography: efficiently estimating many expectation values of an unknown quantum state from randomized measurements using a limited number of copies.
main_result: It establishes that the required sample complexity parameter is governed by graph parameters of the Pauli anticommutation frustration graph, and shows Clifford measurements can be optimal under certain conditions.
method: The problem is reduced to analyzing graph theory invariants (like fractional chromatic number) associated with the frustration graph, utilizing Semidefinite Programming (SDP) hierarchies for computation.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on Pauli observables $\{S_i\}$ acting on $n$ qubits. The setting considers memoryless protocols and measurements restricted to local subsets of qubits (block-limited).
key_observables: Expectation values $	ext{tr}(S_iho)$ for a set of Pauli observables $S=\{S_1, \dots, S_v\}$, and the variance of an estimator $	ext{Var}(\hat{H})$ for Hamiltonian energy estimation.
important_parameters: The sample complexity parameter $\delta(\{S_i\})$, which is bounded by graph parameters like $1/\chi_f(G)$ and $1/\vartheta( ar{G})$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes memoryless measurements and explores the optimality of Clifford measurements, though general cases may require SDP hierarchies.
figures_summary: Table II numerically compares variance bounds for Hamiltonian estimation using various measurement strategies (e.g., single-qubit vs. two-qubit Clifford measurements) across different molecules.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by relating tomography efficiency to graph parameters, derives lower and upper bounds on the sample complexity parameter $\delta$, and applies this framework constructively to estimate molecular Hamiltonian energies with improved variance bounds.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (graph theory, SDP) to quantify resource requirements for quantum state characterization, directly impacting how we design measurements for near-term quantum hardware.
